decision: PHASE 1 CLEAN-BUILD RESET (owner, 2026-10-04): the staging service has no production users, so Phase 1 is a clean build of the FINAL single-host topology and its direct certification, not a continuity-preserving migration. The final topology, the money/security authorities and the $30/month ceiling are unchanged (docs/hosting-budget.md, infra/aws/COST_BUDGET.json).
scope: Every AWS resource the repository's Terraform declares (modules/app, modules/ledger, modules/single-host -- each declaration classified exactly once, pinned by server/src/aws/deploy/migration/phase1CleanBuild.test.ts) and every resource outside this repository's Terraform that its procedures created, depend on or must remove -- including the staging Terraform stacks whose configuration is NOT in this repository (`ownership_forms`, `terraform_states`). Live names are staging's (environment `staging`); another environment substitutes its own. This is the SOURCE classification; P1-R1 confirms it read-only against live AWS and STOPS on any live resource it cannot place here.

ownership_forms.terraform:<app|ledger|single-host>: one of THIS repository's stacks (configuration under infra/aws/stacks; its state listed in terraform_states)
ownership_forms.external-terraform:<stack>: a Terraform stack whose configuration is NOT in this repository (an ops-local checkout); the entry records its state_key, which terraform_states lists. Phase 1 never plans, applies or edits it, except through a separately reviewed change against that stack
ownership_forms.outside-terraform:<who>: not Terraform-managed, as far as the evidence shows
ownership_forms.unresolved:<candidate>|<candidate>: ownership not yet proven: P1-R1 resolves it from the states' contents, and nothing with unresolved ownership is mutated

terraform_states.rule: EVERY Terraform state object P1-R1 finds in the staging state bucket(s) (every .tfstate key, not only the staging prefix) is listed here and mapped to an ownership. An unlisted state is a STOP, exactly like an unplaced AWS resource. The list is not closed: it records what is known. A newly found state is added only by an owner decision and a reviewed amendment, never by R1 itself (for the T3 fast path an owner ruling may first place it provisionally as REVIEW: PHASE1_CLEAN_BUILD.md section 3). A state is read only by its addresses and ids (PHASE1_LEGACY_TEARDOWN.md T0.11: streamed, nothing else kept); never terraform init in infra/aws/stacks/* against another stack's key, never -migrate-state or -force-copy, never a plan or apply of an external stack.
